triples.rationale: Jonah is in the sea creature's belly for three days and three nights. Jesus explicitly cites Jonah's confinement for that duration when comparing it with the Son of Man being in the heart of the earth.
triples.source_text: The Lord commanded a great sea creature to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the sea creature’s belly three days and three nights.

target_units.text: He answered them, “An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, but no sign will be given it except the sign of Jonah the prophet.
For just as Jonah was in the sea creature’s belly three days and three nights, so the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth three days and three nights.

triples.rationale: Jonah prays to the Lord from the sea creature's belly. The psalm describes the dangers of Hades and then a cry for the Lord to rescue the speaker's soul, corresponding to prayer from the peril described by Jonah's surrounding narrative and prayer.
triples.source_text: Jonah prayed to the Lord his God from the sea creature’s belly,

target_units.text: The pangs of death surrounded me; the dangers of Hades found me; I found affliction and pain.
And I called on the name of the Lord: “O Lord, rescue my soul!”

triples.relationship: shared prayer language of affliction and Hades
triples.rationale: Jonah recalls crying in affliction and being heard from the belly of Hades. The psalm likewise joins Hades, affliction, crying to God and God's hearing of the voice from His holy temple.
triples.source_text: and said: “In my affliction I cried to the Lord my God, and He listened to me. From the belly of Hades Thou didst hear the voice of my cry.

target_units.text: The birth pangs of Hades surrounded me; the traps of death overtook me.
And when I was afflicted, I called upon the Lord and cried out to my God. He heard my voice from His holy temple, and my cry before Him will enter His ears.

triples.rationale: Jonah says that all God's billows and waves passed over him in the sea's depth. The psalm uses the same combination of God's billows and waves passing over the speaker in its language of the deep.
triples.source_text: Thou didst cast me into the depths of the heart of the sea, and rivers encircled me. All Thy billows and Thy waves passed over me.

target_units.text: Deep calls upon deep at the sound of Thy waterfalls; all Thy billows and Thy waves passed over me.

triples.relationship: shared lament of exclusion from God's sight
triples.rationale: Jonah says he has been thrust away from God's eyes and asks about looking again toward the holy sanctuary. The psalm similarly recalls the alarmed claim of being cast away from God's eyes, followed by acknowledgment that God heard the petition.
triples.source_text: I said, ‘I have been thrust away from Thine eyes. Shall I again look toward Thy holy sanctuary?’

target_units.text: But I said in my alarm, “So I have been cast away from before Thine eyes.” For this reason Thou heardest the voice of my petition when I cried unto Thee.

triples.rationale: Jonah describes water poured around him as far as his life and the surrounding abyss. The psalm cries for rescue because waters have reached the soul and the speaker has entered the sea's depths, sharing the imagery of life overwhelmed by water.
triples.source_text: Water poured around me up to my life; the uttermost abyss encircled me; my head sank into clefts of mountains.

target_units.text: Save me, God, for waters have entered as far as my soul.
I was stuck in the mud of the depth, with no firm ground; I entered the sea’s depths, and a tempest drowned me.

triples.relationship: descent toward death and appeal for rising
triples.rationale: Jonah describes descent into a land with eternal bars and asks that the ruin of his life rise up. The psalm credits the Lord with bringing the soul up from Hades and saving it from those descending into a pit. The connection is descent toward death and divine rescue; Jonah's supplied petition is preserved as a petition.
triples.source_text: I descended into a land whose bars are everlasting restraints; and let the ruin of my life rise up, Lord my God.

target_units.text: Lord, Thou broughtest my soul up from Hades; Thou didst save me from those descending into a pit.

triples.rationale: Jonah remembers the Lord as his life fails and says his prayer may come into the holy sanctuary. The psalm describes an afflicted cry heard by God from His holy temple, connecting distress with prayer reaching God's dwelling.
triples.source_text: As my life was failing me, I remembered the Lord; may my prayer come to Thee, into Thy holy sanctuary.

target_units.text: And when I was afflicted, I called upon the Lord and cried out to my God. He heard my voice from His holy temple, and my cry before Him will enter His ears.

triples.relationship: remembering God when the soul is troubled
triples.rationale: Jonah remembers the Lord when his life is failing. The psalm likewise connects the soul's trouble with remembering God, giving a close parallel to the prayer's movement from distress to remembrance.
triples.source_text: As my life was failing me, I remembered the Lord; may my prayer come to Thee, into Thy holy sanctuary.

target_units.text: My soul was troubled within me; therefore I will remember Thee from the land of Jordan and Hermoniim, from a small mountain.

triples.rationale: Jonah says that those guarding vain and false things abandoned their mercy. The psalm also speaks of those guarding vanities to no purpose and contrasts that practice with hope in the Lord.
triples.source_text: Those who guard vain and false things abandoned their mercy.

target_units.text: Thou didst hate those who guard vanities to no purpose; but I hoped in the Lord.

triples.relationship: sacrifice of praise and payment of vows
triples.rationale: Jonah promises sacrifice with praise and thanksgiving and payment of his vows. The psalm explicitly commands a sacrifice of praise and payment of vows, followed by the promise of rescue when God is called upon in affliction.
triples.source_text: But I, with a voice of praise and thanksgiving, will sacrifice to Thee. Whatever I vowed I will repay to Thee, for deliverance to the Lord!”

target_units.text: Sacrifice a sacrifice of praise to God and pay your vows to the Most High.
Call on Me in the day of affliction; I will rescue you, and you will glorify Me.” Diapsalma.

triples.rationale: Jonah closes his promise of worship with deliverance directed to the Lord. The psalm directly declares that salvation belongs to the Lord, matching the prayer's attribution of rescue to Him.
triples.source_text: But I, with a voice of praise and thanksgiving, will sacrifice to Thee. Whatever I vowed I will repay to Thee, for deliverance to the Lord!”

target_units.text: Salvation belongs to the Lord, and Thy blessing is upon Thy people.

triples.rationale: The Lord first commands the sea creature to swallow Jonah and later commands it to cast him onto dry land. These two commands frame his confinement and release and show the creature's response to the Lord at both ends of the episode.
triples.source_text: The sea creature was commanded, and it cast Jonah out onto dry land.

target_units.text: The Lord commanded a great sea creature to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the sea creature’s belly three days and three nights.

triples.rationale: The Lord's word comes to Jonah a second time here. The opening verse records the first coming of that word, so the repeated introduction explicitly marks the renewed commission.
triples.source_text: The word of the Lord came to Jonah a second time, saying:

target_units.text: The word of the Lord came to Jonah, the son of Amittai, saying:

triples.rationale: The renewed command sends Jonah to Nineveh and expressly refers to the former proclamation. The opening command names the same city and charges him to proclaim against its wickedness.
triples.source_text: “Rise and go to Nineveh, the great city, and proclaim in it according to the former proclamation that I spoke to you.”

target_units.text: “Rise and go to Nineveh, the great city, and proclaim in it, for the outcry of its wickedness has come up to Me.”

triples.relationship: same-book reversal from flight to obedience
triples.rationale: Jonah now rises and goes to Nineveh according to the Lord's word. Earlier he rose to flee to Tarshish from the Lord's presence; the two departures contrast resistance with obedience to the commission.
triples.source_text: Jonah rose and went to Nineveh as the Lord had spoken. Now Nineveh was a city great before God, about a three-day journey.

target_units.text: But Jonah rose to flee to Tarshish from the presence of the Lord. He went down to Joppa, found a ship traveling to Tarshish, paid its fare and boarded it, to sail with them to Tarshish from the presence of the Lord.

triples.relationship: explicit later reference to Jonah's proclamation
triples.rationale: Jonah's recorded proclamation warns that Nineveh will be overthrown in three more days in this source edition. Matthew explicitly refers to the Ninevites repenting at Jonah's proclamation, identifying the preaching whose effect the narrative records.
triples.source_text: And Jonah began to enter the city, about a day’s journey, and he proclaimed and said, “Three more days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown.”

target_units.text: Men of Nineveh will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at Jonah’s proclamation; and behold, something greater than Jonah is here.

triples.relationship: explicit later reference to Nineveh's repentance
triples.rationale: Nineveh's people believe God and proclaim a fast with sackcloth. Matthew explicitly describes the men of Nineveh as having repented at Jonah's proclamation and makes their response a witness at the judgment.
triples.source_text: The people of Nineveh believed God, proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth, from their greatest to their least.

target_units.text: Men of Nineveh will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at Jonah’s proclamation; and behold, something greater than Jonah is here.
